sources.title: Equality and paired permutation at the additive representation boundary
sources.details: For the same shared projection E, u=v implies uE=vE. Let C be contents, P the position table and Q a row permutation: Q(C+P)=QC+QP. Keeping P fixed yields QC+P, which generally differs and associates each moved content with its destination slot. This concerns representations and associations before other sequence-order-dependent processing.

claims.statement: Identical pixel patches transformed by the same patch embedding have identical content vectors; additive equal-width position vectors can supply slot-specific information.
claims.scope: Content vectors alone under the shared mapping in 10.3; this does not say a program cannot inspect an array index or that addition by itself teaches spatial reasoning.

evidence.supports: Shared linear patch projection and added learnable positional embeddings retain positional information.
Identical patch values produce identical content embeddings under a shared deterministic projection.

claims.statement: The original ones/arange/indexing/addition/tolist/equal fence has position shape (1,4,1), output shape (1,4,3), row0 [1,1,1], row3 [4,4,4], equal False.
claims.scope: One synthetic item, four slots, three dimensionless features. The length-one final position axis broadcasts the slot number to three features. Exact integer-representable float values; no dataset denominator or empirical metric.

evidence.supports: One-filled tensors, exclusive-end arange and dtype inference, broadcasted addition and same-size/value equality semantics.
Actual unchanged fence output matches all displayed results.
Independent exact assertions also check intermediate position shape.

verification.tolerance: Exact shape and value equality; integers 0–4 are exactly representable in float32.

claims.statement: Removing + position leaves both selected rows [1,1,1], changes equal to True and preserves item count and feature width.
claims.scope: Checks the difference between these synthetic vectors before downstream layers; no learning, gradient or accuracy claim.

evidence.supports: All ones at every slot and exact same-size/value comparison.
Actual no-position rows and shape observed.

verification.details: A meaningful bounded change removes addition; verifies position distinction changes while batch and width axes do not.

claims.statement: A formal model can learn positional vectors; index 3 has no inherent lower-right meaning. Patch order, index mapping and training establish spatial associations.
claims.scope: Learned absolute position embeddings in the cited ViT method and this repository, not all possible positional methods. The synthetic scalar ramp is explicitly a separate hand calculation and does not demonstrate useful learned geometry.

evidence.locator: §3.1 pp.3–4 positional embeddings and Inductive bias; Appendix D.4 p.17 raster-order case
evidence.supports: ViT adds learnable 1D embeddings; at initialization they carry no 2D-position information, and spatial relations are learned. D.4 states the default raster-order sequence.
Actual learnable slot vectors are added after the shared projection and paired with raster slots.

claims.statement: Actual VisionEncoder positions are registered trainable parameters with one vector per patch and matching feature width; a four-slot table cannot directly be added to sixteen slots.
claims.scope: Constructor inspection and bounded shape operation only. Reconfiguration or interpolation is a separate operation; no full model evaluation, optimizer or training is performed.

evidence.supports: Assigned module parameters are registered and require gradients by default.
Shape is (1,(image_size//patch_size)^2,width); actual addition occurs after shared projection.
Observed registered requires_grad parameter, (1,4,3) vs (1,16,3) table shapes, expected non-singleton slot-axis mismatch and raw spatial order.

verification.expected: Registered trainable (1,4,3) table for 2×2 patch grid; (1,16,3) for 4×4; direct 4-to-16 addition fails.
verification.observed: Exactly expected; RuntimeError identifies dimension 1 sizes 16 and 4.
verification.details: Instantiated random synthetic encoders only to inspect constructor attributes; no forward of a trained model. Directly tested raw patch raster order and addition mismatch.

claims.statement: Exchanging contents with fixed slot hints relocates contents; moving each content together with its original hint preserves its original spatial association while changing storage order.
claims.scope: The additive content-plus-position representation and original position association. This is not a blanket claim that arbitrary downstream causal masks, extra sequence position encodings, flattening heads, or final decoder outputs are invariant to storage reordering. Distinct contents are used in the check because swapping identical contents is unobservable.

evidence.locator: §3.1 Eq.(1) and Appendix D.4 default raster-order embedding case
evidence.supports: Positions are separate embeddings paired with slot contents before the encoder; raster ordering defines the usual slot mapping.
Paired reordering is exactly a row permutation of existing representations; content-only swap changes position pairing.

Pair reordering is verified at representation boundary, not as universal downstream-output invariance. No GPU, training, model/data download, trained model inference or neural weights saved.
